This work, written in the late 13th or early 14th century, describes her as a noble woman from the city of Vergy in Burgundy, who is converted to Christianity and embarks on a spiritual pilgrimage to the Holy Land.

In the 'Golden Legend' by Jacobus de Voragine, a hagiographical collection of saints' lives, there is a story about a virgin named Catariel. This text was first compiled in the late 13th century, but underwent numerous revisions throughout the Middle Ages. Catariel is said to have lived in Egypt during the time of the Roman persecutions of Christians. She is remembered for her miraculous ability to restore the sight of the blind and for her martyrdom.
